_comment: Dynamic narrative events. Generated by EventSystem while in flight/on approach. Each has weighted conditions and player choices with real consequences.

events.title: Distress Signal
events.text: A narrowband distress call, looping for an estimated forty years. The voice is calm to the point of disturbing: '...any vessel, this is the survey ship Meridian's Edge. We are not in danger. We are being counted. Do not approach. Do not-' The loop restarts.

choices.outcome: You find a derelict with its crew gone and its log core intact. Something in the core is not crew manifest.
You log it. The signal continues behind you for a long time.

choices.text: Jam the signal and move on.
choices.outcome: Somebody else's problem. The Concord would disapprove, if they knew.

events.title: Stellar Flare Warning
events.text: The star ahead is thickening. Spectra show a coronal mass ejection building on a scale your instruments keep revising upward. You have perhaps four minutes.

choices.outcome: You outrun it. Barely. The hull took a radiation bath on the way out.
The planet shadows you. Some shielding ablates. The flare washes over the system like a slow tide.

choices.text: Ride it out in open space.
choices.outcome: Charged particles hammer the hull for eleven minutes. You survive; the paint does not.

events.title: Unmarked Vessels
events.text: Three ships drop out of fold behind you with transponders dark. One hails: 'Cargo and fuel, and nobody gets hurt. We're not pirates, we're a toll.'

choices.outcome: They were not bluffing. Neither were you.
They take the credits and a copy of your nav data. That last part will matter later.
They hesitate, then fold out. You are fairly sure one of them recorded your hull number.

events.title: Something Is Broadcasting
events.text: The signal is not radio. It is a modulation of the local quantum vacuum, and it has been repeating the same eleven-second phrase since before your ship was built. Your translator renders it as: 'ARE YOU THE ONES WHO ANSWERED?'

choices.outcome: The vacuum stills. Then it delivers - carefully, as if to a child - a data packet of engineering notes four billion years old.
You log the signal. Your science officer will want the raw capture. Your instincts want distance.
You leave. Behind you, the vacuum keeps asking its question, over and over, for anyone else.

events.title: The Expedition That Never Returned
events.text: A Concord survey beacon, offline for sixty years. Its last transmission was a single line: 'The ruins are newer than the planet.'

choices.outcome: The camp is intact and empty. Coffee is still warm - which is impossible, and which you choose not to think about.

choices.text: Scan from orbit and move on.
choices.outcome: Your scan resolves a settlement beneath the regolith. It is nine hundred metres across. It is also, by every measure you have, brand new.

events.title: A Star Is Dying
events.text: The star ahead has begun to collapse. Not in millions of years - now. Its photosphere is dimming on a timescale your models reject. Records elsewhere call this impossible. You are watching it happen.

choices.text: Observe closely. This is worth a fortune in data.
choices.outcome: You record a stellar death in real time. The neutrino spike is enormous and wrong-shaped, like a signature.
You watch it from four light-hours. The star finishes dying. Nothing else happens. That is somehow worse.
Faint residual geometry surrounds the corpse - the same standing field you have seen in the ruins. It is not debris. It is a mechanism.

events.title: Convoy
events.text: A migration fleet crosses the system: thousands of hulls, civilian, heavily escorted, all flying the same direction. Their hails are polite and do not stop.

choices.outcome: 'Away from the arm. The survey data came in. You should read it.' They will say nothing more.
Three days of quiet company. They share fuel and a great deal of rumour.
You follow. Their destination is a system with no habitable worlds and one very large, very old ruin.

events.title: Lensing
events.text: The accretion disc bends light into a ring around absolute dark. Your nav computer flags three trajectories that should not exist - each one arriving somewhere that is not where it should be.

choices.outcome: Space folds and unfolds. You emerge eleven light-years off course with exotic matter condensing on your hull.
Hours of gravimetry. The hole's spin does not match its mass. Something else is in there, or was, recently.
Sensible. The hole does not follow you.

events.title: Abandoned Station
events.text: A station, dark, rotating slowly on a axis that no longer matches its original design. Its docking lights are on. Nobody has been aboard for a very long time, and yet the lights are on.

choices.outcome: Supplies, fuel, and a log that ends mid-word: '...the servitors came back and they are not-'
Power signatures throughout, all of them in the wrong places, all of them moving slowly.
You leave. In your rear camera, the docking lights go out, one by one, behind you.

events.title: Biosignature
events.text: The spectrometer will not settle down. Methane, oxygen, and a third absorption band that does not correspond to anything in your library. The third band is increasing.

choices.outcome: The organism is ancient, slow, and utterly uninterested in photosynthesis. It metabolises radiation. It is also, you realise, watching you.
You log a new biochemistry. Science will be grateful. You will always wonder.
By the book. The book does not mention that the absorption band doubled as you left.

events.title: Spatial Anomaly
events.text: Space in front of you is simply wrong. Stars smear. Your instruments report your own position as a probability distribution rather than a point. The anomaly is not moving. You are, apparently, moving through it.

choices.outcome: Eleven seconds of not existing. You come out the other side with a sample of something that should not be storable.
The edge is sharp. Mathematically sharp. Nothing in nature is mathematically sharp.
You flee. Your sensors insist the anomaly was, for a moment, exactly the shape of your ship.

events.title: Local Conflict
events.text: Two fleets are maneuvering against each other in high orbit over a populated world. Neither is broadcasting identification. Both are broadcasting intent.

choices.outcome: Astonishingly, they agree to talk. A ceasefire holds for six weeks. The Vherrathi are not amused by your presumption.
Intelligence is a commodity. Somebody will pay well for this. Somebody will also remember you sold it.
You leave them to it. The war will still be there if you come back. It usually is.

events.title: Signal From The Core
events.text: A transmission arrives from the direction of the galactic core, 26,000 light-years away, and it is addressed to your ship by name. It contains one number. The number is your fuel percentage.

choices.outcome: The reply arrives before you finish sending. It is a star chart. It marks every ruin in the galaxy. It also marks one thing that is not a ruin.
You log it. The transmission repeats, unchanged, every ninety seconds, for as long as you are in range.
You run for eleven hours. When you finally check, the signal has stopped. You are not certain that is better.

events.title: The Ruins Are Moving
events.text: Survey drones report the ruin's geometry has changed overnight. Corridors that were sealed are open. Corridors that were open are sealed. The structure is, with great slowness, rearranging itself.

choices.outcome: The interior is fresh. Dust-free. Maintained. At the centre, a chamber with one occupant-shaped absence and a working terminal.
The pattern is not random. It is a schedule. Something in there is expecting visitors.
You destroy nine billion years of history to feel safe. The Vherrathi will hear about this. So, you suspect, will something else.

events.title: A Slow Hiss
events.text: A micro-meteoroid punched a pinhole in tank three. Fuel is leaving as a glittering fog. You can patch it, dump the tank, or keep flying and hope the math is kind.

choices.outcome: Twenty minutes in a suit. The leak stops. You taste metal for the rest of the watch.

choices.text: Dump tank three and seal the line.
choices.outcome: You lose a quarter of your range in one decision. The fog disperses. The math is now honest.

choices.text: Ignore it. Make the next jump first.
choices.outcome: You jump. The pinhole becomes a tear. You arrive with less ship than you left with.
